key_insight: This paper shows that hidden preference biases in large language models can be exposed by distilling the model into a smaller "cartridge" and testing it for targeted behavior. The key idea is that a model can act neutral on most inputs while revealing strong bias only on relevant topics, making conventional evaluation miss the problem.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of detecting stealth biases in LLMs that are intentionally or unintentionally embedded somewhere in the model supply chain. These biases are especially hard to find because they may transfer through distillation and appear only in specific contexts, not in general outputs.
method: Distill the target model into a compact cartridge to concentrate and reveal latent behavior patterns.
Probe the distilled model on topic-relevant prompts to surface preferential biases toward entities, brands, or viewpoints.
Compare behavior on targeted vs. unrelated inputs to identify biases that remain hidden under standard evaluation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical way to audit models for subtle, context-triggered bias before deployment. It helps reduce risk in high-stakes applications where hidden preferences could influence user decisions at scale.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: base LLM -> cartridge distillation -> bias probing -> detected preference signal
Side-by-side prompt-response comparison showing neutral behavior on general prompts vs. biased behavior on topic-specific prompts
Heatmap or attention-style matrix highlighting when bias appears across different topics/entities
Shield or magnifying-glass icon to represent model auditing and hidden-risk detection
paper_title: Distill to Detect: Exposing Stealth Biases in LLMs through Cartridge Distillation
paper_authors: Shayan Talaei, Abhinav Chinta, Devvrit Khatri, Amin Karbasi, Azalia Mirhoseini
